newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Charges force Swiss Ascom into red.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Charges force Swiss Ascom into red.

text.p: Swiss telecommunications group Ascom Holding AG said on Wednesday that restructuring provisions had slashed 1996 results to a net loss of 128 million francs ($87.3 million) and forced it to omit a dividend payment again.
Ascom resumed paying a dividend only last year after a three-year break. But it said underlying operating profit rose strongly in 1996 for a third year, gaining 25 percent to 94 million francs.
Chairman Felix Wittlin said he saw the company returning to net profit in 1997, but declined at a news conference to make a specific forecast.

"To enable Ascom to intensify its focus on selected segments of telecommunications and serve automation unimpeded by past constraints, 152 million francs (in) restructuring costs were charged to income in 1996," Ascom said in a statement.
Ascom did not say what the restructuring provisions would pay for.
It said the company had proposed waiving a dividend again after paying 25 francs per bearer share last year on 1995 results.
"Incoming orders in the first quarter of 1997 were clearly higher than the corresponding year-ago quarter, while sales were slightly lower," Ascom said.
Net debt was reduced last year by 26 percent to 470 million francs, cutting the level to half of 1993 levels.
"Industry orders and revenue showed little change on the previous year's figures despite an industry-average fall in prices," Ascom said.
Orders fell 1.8 percent to 2.77 billion francs while sales eased slightly to 2.94 billion from 2.96 billion francs in 1995.
Ascom's biggest division, telecommunications, increased operating profit to 115 million francs from 113 million although sales rose only 0.1 percent to 2.10 billion.

Service automation, the other main business whose products include ticket systems, banking automation and smartcard-operated payphones, saw sales slip to 866 million francs from 869 million million but operating profit gain to 38 million from 23 million.

Separately, Ascom said it had agreed to sell Nexicon, a small U.S. subsidiary developing a universal telecommunications switch to intergrate computer networks, to an undisclosed company, pending regulatory approval.
Ascom also said it had taken over a 40 percent stake from Sweden's Ericsson in a joint venture they set up in 1995 in on-site paging. It provided no details. ($ = 1.466 Swiss Francs)
